# Adjudication Task — Chapter 622

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃622화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|순수하게 무림에서 보낸 시간만 따져도 어언 1년이 훌쩍 넘었다.
  6|
  7|뜻하지 않게 여러 사건에 얽히다 보니 산서성을 벗어나 타지를 전전하게 되었고, 그 과정에서 숱한 인간 군상과 그들이 속한 문파를 방문하기도 했다.
  8|
  9|하지만 단언컨대, 그 어떤 거대 문파라 해도 지금 내 눈 앞에 펼쳐진 광경과는 비교조차 할 수 없을 것이다.
 10|
 11|“허.”
 12|
 13|“미친…….”
 14|
 15|곳곳에서 탄성이 터져 나왔다.
 16|
 17|산봉우리에서 봤을 때도 엄청난 면적이라는 건 알았지만 이 정도일 줄이야.
 18|
 19|운무(雲霧)가 사라지고 목적지에 점점 가까워질수록 내 입도 점점 더 크게 벌어졌다.
 20|
 21|‘아니, 이게 문파라고?’
 22|
 23|두 가지 의미로 놀라웠다.
 24|
 25|첫 번째 놀라움은 앞서 말했듯이 그 광활함에서 오는 것이었고, 두 번째는…….
 26|
 27|
 28|
 29|남만야수궁(南蠻野獸宮)
 30|
 31|
 32|
 33|광활한 면적을 둘러싼 울타리와 누군가 엉성한 글씨체로 휘갈겨 쓴 목판 때문이었다.
 34|
 35|높고 단단한 성벽이나 철문이 아니라, 말 그대로 울타리다. 울타리.
 36|
 37|‘……아니. 이게 문파라고?’
 38|
 39|같은 생각. 다른 의미.
 40|
 41|심지어 울타리가 멀쩡한 것도 아니다.
 42|
 43|반쯤 허물어진 울타리를 보며 잠깐 생각에 잠겨 있던 내가 남호를 향해 물었다.
 44|
 45|“남 노인, 설마 여기가 진짜…….”
 46|
 47|“남만야수궁이 맞냐고?”
 48|
 49|“아, 예.”
 50|
 51|내가 고개를 끄덕이자, 남호가 담담하게 입을 열었다.
 52|
 53|“자네, 글 읽을 줄은 아나?”
 54|
 55|“당연하죠.”
 56|
 57|“그럼 저 글씨 좀 읽어 보게. 아니, 내가 대신 읽어 주는 게 낫겠군.”
 58|
 59|남호가 엉성한 글씨로 적힌 표지만을 가리키며 말을 이었다.
 60|
 61|“남. 만. 야. 수. 궁.”
 62|
 63|“…….”
 64|
 65|“적힌 그대로일세. 이곳부터가 남만야수궁이야.”
 66|
 67|알긴 안다. 머릿속에 예상했던 그림을 아득히 벗어나서 문제지.
 68|
 69|위에서 언뜻 봤을 때는 엄청 거대한 건축물이 있나 보다, 싶었는데 막상 안개를 벗어나 가까운 곳에서 목격하니 이건 숫제 허허벌판이 아닌가.
 70|
 71|“조장님, 남만야수궁이 아니라 그냥 남만목장 아닙니까? 사방에 울타리만 쳐져 있고.”
 72|
 73|주위를 둘러보던 주화란도 혁무진의 떨떠름한 말에 고개를 끄덕였다.
 74|
 75|“저도 남만야수궁은 처음이라 잘은 모르겠지만…… 궁이라고 부르기에는 손색이 있긴 하네요.”
 76|
 77|묵묵히 상황을 지켜보던 송일섬과 사마표도 한마디씩 보탰다.
 78|
 79|“확실히 이상한 부분이 있구려.”
 80|
 81|“혁무진의 말대로 사람이 안 보인다는 점이 걸리는군. 그렇다고 다른 전각이나 건물이 있는 것도 아니고. 그렇지 않으냐, 태산?”
 82|
 83|“주군. 태산이 배고프다. 저 버섯 먹어도 되나?”
 84|
 85|사마표가 단번에 고개를 저었다.
 86|
 87|“안 된다.”
 88|
 89|“그럼 소는? 저기 걸어가는 소가 맛있어 보인다.”
 90|
 91|“흑룡마문의 소문주라고 했나? 이건 부탁인데, 저 금수만도 못한 놈 주둥이 좀 틀어막게. 한 번 더 들으면 복장 터져서 죽을 것 같으니까.”
 92|
 93|“……알겠소.”
 94|
 95|“하나 더. 지금 눈에 보이는 모든 풀과 짐승들은 남만야수궁의 것일세. 부디 잊지 말라고. 터지기 직전의 내 복장도.”
 96|
 97|부쩍 늙은 얼굴로 사마표에게 엄중한 경고를 날린 남호가, 광활한 대지를 가리키며 말을 이었다.
 98|
 99|“그리고 자네들의 생각은 충분히 이해하네만, 나는 이곳이 남만야수궁이라고 한 적은 없네.”
100|
101|“예? 아까 분명 그러셨는데요.”
102|
103|“아닐세.”
104|
105|“아, 혹시 노망나셨습니까?”
106|
107|“…….”
108|
109|표정이 급격히 어두워지는 것을 보니 확실하다. 나는 측은지심을 담아 남호를 바라보았다.
110|
111|“저런. 그래도 괜찮을 겁니다. 저와 가까운 지인 중에도 노환으로 고생하셨던 분이 있는데, 지금은 거의 다 나으셨거든요.”
112|
113|“먼저 세 가지를 말하고 싶군. 첫째, 난 노환이 아닐세. 둘째. 이건 듣는 와중에 살짝 궁금해져서 묻는 건데, 자네 지인이라는 그분은 어떻게 노환을 이겨 낸 건가?”
114|
115|“반로환동이요.”
116|
117|“……그거 아주 좋은 방법이로군. 내가 무공을 익히지 않은 여든 살 노인이라는 것만 빼면.”
118|
119|“원래 인생은 여든부터 아닙니까.”
120|
121|“자네 인생을 여기에서 끝내고 싶지만, 힘이 없으니 참겠네.”
122|
123|솟구치는 울화를 삭힌 남호가 말을 이었다.
124|
125|“마지막 세 번째는 앞서 했던 말과 동일하네. 나는 이곳이 남만야수궁이라는 말을 한 적이 없어. ‘이곳부터’ 남만야수궁이라고 했지.”
126|
127|“아.”
128|
129|비슷하지만 의미는 확실히 다르다.
130|
131|이제야 남호의 말이 의미하는 바를 깨달은 내가 되물었다.
132|
133|“그럼?”
134|
135|“맞네. 이곳은 남만야수궁의 지배하에 놓인 땅 중 하나일세. 남만의 다른 지역과는 달리 궁주가 직접 다스리는 직할지(直轄地)라고 하면 더 이해하기 쉽겠군.”
136|
137|“황제가 천하 곳곳에 번왕(藩王)이나 성주를 두는 것과 비슷한 느낌이군요. 이곳은 한 나라의 수도인 셈이고.”
138|
139|“정확하네. 물론 궁주의 권위가 천자에 미치지 못하고, 남만에 존재하는 여러 부족장의 권위는 성주 이상이라는 차이가 있긴 하지만.”
140|
141|남호의 이야기를 듣고 있던 주화란이 나직한 탄성과 함께 입을 열었다.
142|
143|“그러고 보니 오래전 조부님께서 남긴 기록에서 그런 글귀를 읽은 적이 있어요. 남만은 하나의 왕국이며, 남만야수궁은 다섯 개의 현읍을 아우르는 거대한 목장과 같다고.”
144|
145|“표왕의 손녀답군. 하지만 그 주공산 대협도 이 울타리 너머까지 도달한 적은 없다네. 이민족이 아닌 이들은 출입할 수 없거든.”
146|
147|“그 정도입니까?”
148|
149|“그 정도일세.”
150|
151|남호의 말이 사실이라면, 폐쇄성으로는 천하에서 둘째가라면 서러운 문파인 사천당가도 남만야수궁에는 한 수 접어줘야 한다.
152|
153|혀를 내두른 나는 끝없이 늘어선 울타리와 목초지 너머를 바라보았다.
154|
155|“그런데 저희는 들어가야 하잖습니까.”
156|
157|“그렇지.”
158|
159|“다른 방법이라도 있습니까? 혹시 남 노인께서는 이민족이니까 출입이 가능…….”
160|
161|“외지인의 출입이 불가능하다고 했지, 이민족이라고 해서 출입이 쉽다고 한 기억은 없네만.”
162|
163|“아.”
164|
165|“이곳에서 나는 그저 힘없고 평범한 묘족 늙은이일 뿐일세. 만약 암천이 천하에 마수를 뻗지 않았고, 자네들이 찾아오지 않았다면 조용히 생을 마감했을…… 호로 새끼!”
166|
167|남호의 갑작스러운 호통에 깜짝 놀란 나는 눈을 크게 떴다.
168|
169|“아니, 남 노인. 왜 자책을 하세요. 조용히 생을 마감한다고 호로 새끼라니.”
170|
171|“나 말고! 저 새끼! 저 시벌 호로 새끼 붙잡아!”
172|
173|금방이라도 숨이 넘어갈 듯한 남호의 외침에 고개를 돌린 우리는, 울타리를 넘어 엉금엉금 기어가는 커다란 궁둥이를 볼 수 있었다.
174|
175|그 앞에서 평화롭게 풀을 뜯고 있는 누런 송아지 한 마리도.
176|
177|“어. 어어?”
178|
179|“저놈, 설마.”
180|
181|“저 새끼 언제 저기까지 갔어!”
182|
183|“태 소협!”
184|
185|“태산아!”
186|
187|사람들의 목소리에 이어, 마지막으로 울려 퍼진 사마표의 부르짖음에 태산이 움찔한 그 순간.
188|
189|음머?
190|
191|이상함을 알아차린 송아지가 번쩍 고개를 치켜들었다.
192|
193|어느새 가까워진 태산의 모습에 커다랗고 맑은 눈망울에 느낌표가 떠올랐고, 동시에 아직 완전히 자라지 않은 발굽이 풀을 밟았다.
194|
195|타다닥!
196|
197|빠른 상황 판단과 도주 시도. 그러나 송아지보다 태산이 한발 빨랐다.
198|
199|“소고기! 거기 딱 서라!”
200|
201|굳은 의지가 담긴 외침과 함께 태산의 거대한 덩치가 허공을 날았다.
202|
203|호랑이나 표범 같은 맹수도 아니고, 덜 자란 송아지가 어떻게 작정하고 움직인 절정 고수를 피하겠나.
204|
205|쿵, 하는 둔중한 소리와 함께 밑에 깔린 송아지가 비명을 질렀다.
206|
207|음머어어어!
208|
209|듣기만 해도 눈시울이 축축해지는 애달픈 울음소리였지만, 연이은 강행군과 적량 배식으로 뱃가죽이 뒤집힌 태산에게는 입가가 축축해질 만한 소리였다.
210|
211|“태산이! 소고기!”
212|
213|“당장 저 새끼 붙잡아!”
214|
215|남호의 외침이 끝나기도 전, 이미 울타리를 넘어 쇄도한 내 신형은 태산의 코앞까지 도달해 있었다.
216|
217|덥석.
218|
219|“놔라! 소고기 육회!”
220|
221|“그만해. 이 피도 눈물도 없는 미친놈아. 워낭소리도 못 봤어?”
222|
223|“못 봤다!”
224|
225|“……아.”
226|
227|그건 그렇겠네.
228|
229|순간 납득이 되긴 했지만 그건 그거고 이건 이거다. 단번에 태산의 뒷덜미를 잡아챈 나는 적당히 힘을 주어 뒤로 당겼다.
230|
231|산만 한 덩치가 뒤로 나동그라지자 겨우 살아난 소고기. 아니, 송아지가 벌떡 일어나 달리기 시작했다.
232|
233|두두두두!
234|
235|사정없이 뒤집히는 풀과 일어나는 먼지.
236|
237|꽁무니가 빠져라 목초리를 벗어나는 송아지의 엉덩이를 바라보며, 태산이 구슬프게 중얼거렸다.
238|
239|“안 된다. 태산이 우둔살…….”
240|
241|이 새끼는 고향이 무슨 마장동인가.
242|
243|내가 녀석의 출신 성분을 의심하고 있던 그때, 남호가 불같은 외침과 함께 길길이 날뛰었다.
244|
245|“노옴!”
246|
247|“남 노인. 진정하세요, 진정.”
248|
249|“지금 진정하게 생겼나! 남만야수궁의 영역에서는 아무것도 건드리지 말라고 그토록 신신당부했거늘! 이 덩치 큰 식충이 새끼가 어른 말을 귓등으로도 안 듣고 사고를 쳐?”
250|
251|황급히 달려온 사마표가 남호와 태산 사이를 가로막았다.
252|
253|“미안하오, 남 노인. 내가 잠시 한눈을 판 사이에 그만…… 태산이 네 이 녀석, 당장 사과드리지 못하겠느냐.”
254|
255|태산이 남호를 똑바로 바라보며 대답했다.
256|
257|“태산이. 배고프다.”
258|
259|“저 씨벌놈이. 당장 이 손 놓게. 놔. 안 놔? 내가 이 꼴 보려고 남만에서 오십 년 넘게 모기 물려 가며 기다린 줄 알아?”
260|
261|역시 인생은 여든부터가 확실하다. 무공도 안 익혔으면서 적천강도 한 수 접어들 정도의 기세를 뿜어내는 남호만 봐도 알 수 있었다.
262|
263|활화산처럼 날뛰던 늙은 은영각 요원이 진정한 것은 그로부터 일각이 흐른 뒤였다.
264|
265|“후. 이제 괜찮아졌으니 손 놓게.”
266|
267|“정말 괜찮으신 거 맞습니까?”
268|
269|“잠깐 사이에 오장육부가 한 바퀴 뒤집히긴 했는데, 당장 죽을 정도는 아닐세.”
270|
271|180도 돌았다면 문제가 있지만 360도는 인정이지.
272|
273|고개를 끄덕인 내 눈짓에 혁무진이 손을 놓자, 남호가 임종을 앞둔 얼굴로 한숨을 내쉬었다.
274|
275|“그래, 그나마 아무 일도 없었으니 다행이지. 남만야수궁의 인물이 그 꼴을 봤었다면 초장부터 일이 어긋났을 게야.”
276|

[P86]
“Young Hero Tae!”

[P87]
“Taishan!”

[P88]
Sama Pyo’s cry came last. Taishan flinched.

[P89]
*Moo?*

[P90]
The calf sensed something was wrong and jerked its head up. Taishan was already close. An exclamation mark seemed to appear in its large, clear eyes as its not-yet-fully-grown hooves dug into the grass.

[P91]
*Pat-pat-pat!*

[P92]
A quick decision and an attempt to flee—but Taishan was a step faster.

[P93]
“Beef! Stop right there!”

[P94]
With that determined shout, his enormous body flew through the air.

[P95]
The calf was no tiger or leopard. How was it supposed to evade a Peak master who’d decided to catch it?

[P96]
Taishan landed with a heavy *thud*, and the calf pinned beneath him screamed.

[P97]
*Moooooo!*

[P98]
It was a plaintive cry, enough to bring tears to your eyes just hearing it. But after days of forced marches and meager rations, all it did was make Taishan’s mouth water.

[P99]
“Taishan! Beef!”

[P100]
“Get that bastard off it!”

[P101]
Before Namho finished shouting, I’d vaulted the fence and reached Taishan.

[P102]
I grabbed him.

[P103]
“Let go! Beef tartare!”

[P104]
“Stop it, you heartless lunatic. Haven’t you seen *The Sound of the Bell*?”[^1]

[P105]
“No!”

[P106]
“…Ah.”

[P107]
Well, of course he hadn’t.

[P108]
That made sense, but it changed nothing. I seized him by the back of the neck and hauled him away.

[P109]
His mountain-sized body toppled backward. The beef—no, the calf—scrambled to its feet and ran.

[P110]
*Thud-thud-thud-thud!*

[P111]
Grass flew up beneath its hooves, dust rising in its wake. Taishan watched its rump disappear beyond the pasture and muttered mournfully.

[P112]
“No. Taishan’s rump meat…”

[P113]
*Was this guy born in Majang-dong or something?*[^2]

[P114]
While I questioned his origins, Namho erupted.

[P115]
“You brute!”

[P116]
“Elder Namho, calm down. Please.”

[P117]
“How am I supposed to calm down? I warned you again and again not to touch anything on the Nanman Beast Palace’s land! That great hulking glutton ignored every word I said and went after a calf?”

[P118]
Sama Pyo hurried between Namho and Taishan.

[P119]
“I’m sorry, Elder Namho. I looked away for just a moment, and… Taishan, apologize to him at once.”

[P120]
Taishan looked Namho straight in the eye.

[P121]
“Taishan is hungry.”

[P122]
“That fucking bastard. Let go of my hand. Let go! Are you going to let go or not? Did you think I spent over fifty years getting bitten by mosquitoes in Nanman just to see this?”

[P123]
Life really did begin at eighty. Namho had never learned martial arts, yet the aura he was giving off might have made even Jeok Cheongang back down for once.

[P124]
The old Hidden Shadow Pavilion agent raged like an active volcano for another fifteen minutes before finally calming down.

[P125]
“Whew. I’m fine now. Let go of my hand.”

[P126]
“Are you sure?”

[P127]
“My insides have turned a full circle, but I’m not about to die.”

[P128]
A 180-degree turn would have been a problem. A full 360? That was fine.

[P129]
I nodded to Hyuk Mujin, and he released Namho’s hand. Namho sighed, looking as though he were on his deathbed.

[P130]
“At least nothing happened in the end. If someone from the Nanman Beast Palace had seen that, we’d have been in trouble before we even began.”

[P131]
At another sect in the Central Plains, someone might have thought, *It’s only one cow.* But cultures and people differed. Just as nomads treasured their horses like their own lives, livestock was a valuable asset here, where the boundaries between tribes were sharply drawn and relations between them often strained.

[P132]
*It’s called the Nanman Beast Palace, after all.*

[P133]
Even the name sounded animal-friendly. Namho had warned us from the start not to touch anything for a reason.

[P134]
“So what do we do now?” Hyuk Mujin asked. “We can’t wait here forever for someone to show up.”

[P135]
“Entering the Nanman Beast Palace’s territory without permission would cause trouble. We’ll have to find another way.”

[P136]
Namho reached into his bundle and took something out.

[P137]
“What’s that?”

[P138]
“An emergency signal firework. If it goes off, someone should at least come out to investigate.”

[P139]
He smiled confidently and lit the fuse with his fire striker.

[P140]
*Crackle.*

[P141]
The fuse burned rapidly toward the end. Then, with a tremendous noise, the firework shot upward.

[P142]
*Fwoooosh—boom!*

[P143]
The problem was that its sparks fell onto the pasture instead of scattering harmlessly in the air.

[P144]
“…Huh?”

[P145]
“…Huh?”

[P146]
*Whoooosh—roar!*

[P147]
The pasture went up in flames. Around me, everyone stood stunned.

[P148]
I watched the livestock flee in every direction and muttered, “…Someone will definitely come out now.”

[P149]
“…That wasn’t supposed to happen.”

[P150]
Wasn’t supposed to happen, my ass. We were fucked.

[P151]
I stared miserably at the burning pasture.

[P152]
*Roooar!*

[P153]
A savage roar rang out, and a figure appeared beyond the hill on the far side of the flames.

[P154]
[^1]: *The Sound of the Bell* is a Korean documentary film about an elderly farmer and his ox.

[P155]
[^2]: Majang-dong is a Seoul district known for its livestock and meat markets.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

He pointed at the clumsily lettered board.

[P27]
“Nan. Man. Beast. Palace.”

[P28]
“…”

[P29]
“That’s what it says. The Nanman Beast Palace begins here.”

[P30]
I knew what the sign said. The problem was how far the place was from anything I’d imagined.

[P31]
From above, I’d thought there must be an enormous building here. But up close, out of the mist, it was practically an empty field.

[P32]
“Captain, shouldn’t we call this the Nanman Ranch instead of the Nanman Beast Palace? All I see are fences.”

[P33]
Ju Hwaran looked around and nodded at Hyuk Mujin’s dubious assessment.

[P34]
“This is my first time here, so I can’t say I know much about the Nanman Beast Palace, but… it does seem a little lacking for a palace.”

[P35]
Song Ilseom and Sama Pyo, who had been watching in silence, each weighed in.

[P36]
“There’s certainly something strange about it.”

[P37]
“As Hyuk Mujin said, the lack of people bothers me. I don’t see any other pavilions or buildings, either. What do you think, Taishan?”

[P38]
“My lord. Taishan is hungry. Can Taishan eat that mushroom?”

[P39]
Sama Pyo shook his head at once.

[P40]
“No.”

[P41]
“Then the cow? That cow walking over there looks tasty.”

[P42]
“You’re the Young Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate, aren’t you? Do me a favor and shut that brute’s mouth. If I hear one more word, I think I’ll burst a blood vessel and die.”

[P43]
“…I understand.”

[P44]
“One more thing. Every blade of grass and every animal you can see belongs to the Nanman Beast Palace. Please remember that. And remember I’m about to burst a blood vessel.”

[P45]
Looking considerably older than he had a moment ago, Namho gave Sama Pyo that stern warning, then pointed across the vast grounds.

[P46]
“I understand why you’re confused, but I never said this place *was* the Nanman Beast Palace.”

[P47]
“What? You said exactly that a moment ago.”

[P48]
“No, I didn’t.”

[P49]
“Ah. Have you gone senile?”

[P50]
“…”

[P51]
His expression darkened so quickly that it seemed certain. I gave him a sympathetic look.

[P52]
“Oh dear. Still, I’m sure you’ll be all right. Someone close to me suffered from the infirmities of old age too, and he’s almost completely recovered.”

[P53]
“Three things. First, I do not suffer from the infirmities of old age. Second—and I ask only because you’ve made me curious—how did this acquaintance of yours recover?”

[P54]
“He Returned to Youth.”

[P55]
“…An excellent method. Apart from the fact that I’m an eighty-year-old man who’s never learned martial arts.”

[P56]
“Isn’t eighty when life begins?”

[P57]
“I’d like to end *your* life here, but I lack the strength.”

[P58]
Namho swallowed his anger and went on.

[P59]
“Third, what I said before still stands. I never said this place *was* the Nanman Beast Palace. I said the Nanman Beast Palace begins *here*.”

[P60]
“Oh.”

[P61]
Similar words, very different meanings. Now that I understood, I asked, “So what is this place?”

[P62]
“One of the lands under the Nanman Beast Palace’s rule. Unlike the rest of Nanman, it’s governed directly by the Palace Lord. Does that make more sense?”

[P63]
“Like the Emperor appointing vassal kings and City Lords throughout the realm. This place is effectively the capital.”

[P64]
“Exactly. Of course, the Palace Lord doesn’t have the authority of the Son of Heaven, and Nanman’s tribal chiefs have more authority than City Lords.”

[P65]
Ju Hwaran, who had been listening, gave a quiet exclamation.

[P66]
“Now that you mention it, I remember reading something like that in my grandfather’s records. He wrote that Nanman was a single kingdom, and the Nanman Beast Palace was like an enormous ranch spanning five counties.”

[P67]
“As expected of the Escort King’s granddaughter. But even Great Hero Ju Gongsan never crossed this fence. People who aren’t of Nanman’s ethnic groups aren’t allowed inside.”

[P68]
“It’s that strict?”

[P69]
“It is.”

[P70]
If Namho was telling the truth, even the Sichuan Tang Clan—a sect as closed to outsiders as any in the world—had to yield to the Nanman Beast Palace.

[P71]
I shook my head and looked past the seemingly endless fence and pasture.

[P72]
“But we need to get in.”

[P73]
“Yes.”

[P74]
“Is there another way? Since you’re Miao, perhaps you can enter…”

[P75]
“I said outsiders aren’t allowed in. I don’t recall saying it was easy for the local peoples, either.”

[P76]
“Oh.”

[P77]
“Here, I’m nothing more than an ordinary, powerless old Miao man. If Dark Heaven hadn’t reached its claws across the world, and you hadn’t come looking for me, I would have quietly lived out my days… You son of a bitch!”

[P78]
I flinched at his sudden shout.

[P79]
“Elder Namho, why are you calling yourself that? What’s wrong with quietly living out your days?”

[P80]
“Not me! That bastard! Catch that fucking son of a bitch!”

[P81]
At Namho’s frantic yell, we turned.

[P82]
A huge backside was crawling over the fence. Beyond it, a yellow calf grazed peacefully.

[P83]
“Oh. Oh, no.”

[P84]
“Surely he isn’t…”

[P85]
“When did that bastard get over there?”

[P86]
“Young Hero Tae!”

[P87]
“Taishan!”

[P88]
Sama Pyo’s cry came last. Taishan flinched.

[P89]
*Moo?*

[P90]
The calf sensed something was wrong and jerked its head up. Taishan was already close. An exclamation mark seemed to appear in its large, clear eyes as its not-yet-fully-grown hooves dug into the grass.

[P91]
*Pat-pat-pat!*

[P92]
A quick decision and an attempt to flee—but Taishan was a step faster.

[P93]
“Beef! Stop right there!”

[P94]
With that determined shout, his enormous body flew through the air.

[P95]
The calf was no tiger or leopard. How was it supposed to evade a Peak master who’d decided to catch it?

[P96]
Taishan landed with a heavy *thud*, and the calf pinned beneath him screamed.

[P97]
*Moooooo!*

[P98]
It was a plaintive cry, enough to bring tears to your eyes just hearing it. But after days of forced marches and meager rations, all it did was make Taishan’s mouth water.

[P99]
“Taishan! Beef!”

[P100]
“Get that bastard off it!”

[P101]
Before Namho finished shouting, I’d vaulted the fence and reached Taishan.

[P102]
I grabbed him.

[P103]
“Let go! Beef tartare!”

[P104]
“Stop it, you heartless lunatic. Haven’t you seen *The Sound of the Bell*?”[^1]

[P105]
“No!”

[P106]
“…Ah.”

[P107]
Well, of course he hadn’t.

[P108]
That made sense, but it changed nothing. I seized him by the back of the neck and hauled him away.

[P109]
His mountain-sized body toppled backward. The beef—no, the calf—scrambled to its feet and ran.

[P110]
*Thud-thud-thud-thud!*

[P111]
Grass flew up beneath its hooves, dust rising in its wake. Taishan watched its rump disappear beyond the pasture and muttered mournfully.

[P112]
“No. Taishan’s rump meat…”

[P113]
*Was this guy born in Majang-dong or something?*[^2]

[P114]
While I questioned his origins, Namho erupted.

[P115]
“You brute!”

[P116]
“Elder Namho, calm down. Please.”

[P117]
“How am I supposed to calm down? I warned you again and again not to touch anything on the Nanman Beast Palace’s land! That great hulking glutton ignored every word I said and went after a calf?”

[P118]
Sama Pyo hurried between Namho and Taishan.

[P119]
“I’m sorry, Elder Namho. I looked away for just a moment, and… Taishan, apologize to him at once.”

[P120]
Taishan looked Namho straight in the eye.

[P121]
“Taishan is hungry.”

[P122]
“That fucking bastard. Let go of my hand. Let go! Are you going to let go or not? Did you think I spent over fifty years getting bitten by mosquitoes in Nanman just to see this?”

[P123]
Life really did begin at eighty. Namho had never learned martial arts, yet the aura he was giving off might have made even Jeok Cheongang back down for once.

[P124]
The old Hidden Shadow Pavilion agent raged like an active volcano for another fifteen minutes before finally calming down.

[P125]
“Whew. I’m fine now. Let go of my hand.”

[P126]
“Are you sure?”

[P127]
“My insides have turned a full circle, but I’m not about to die.”

[P128]
A 180-degree turn would have been a problem. A full 360? That was fine.

[P129]
I nodded to Hyuk Mujin, and he released Namho’s hand. Namho sighed, looking as though he were on his deathbed.

[P130]
“At least nothing happened in the end. If someone from the Nanman Beast Palace had seen that, we’d have been in trouble before we even began.”

[P131]
At another sect in the Central Plains, someone might have thought, *It’s only one cow.* But cultures and people differed. Just as nomads treasured their horses like their own lives, livestock was a valuable asset here, where the boundaries between tribes were sharply drawn and relations between them often strained.

[P132]
*It’s called the Nanman Beast Palace, after all.*

[P133]
Even the name sounded animal-friendly. Namho had warned us from the start not to touch anything for a reason.

[P134]
“So what do we do now?” Hyuk Mujin asked. “We can’t wait here forever for someone to show up.”

[P135]
“Entering the Nanman Beast Palace’s territory without permission would cause trouble. We’ll have to find another way.”

[P136]
Namho reached into his bundle and took something out.

[P137]
“What’s that?”

[P138]
“An emergency signal firework. If it goes off, someone should at least come out to investigate.”

[P139]
He smiled confidently and lit the fuse with his fire striker.

[P140]
*Crackle.*

[P141]
The fuse burned rapidly toward the end. Then, with a tremendous noise, the firework shot upward.

[P142]
*Fwoooosh—boom!*

[P143]
The problem was that its sparks fell onto the pasture instead of scattering harmlessly in the air.

[P144]
“…Huh?”

[P145]
“…Huh?”

[P146]
*Whoooosh—roar!*

[P147]
The pasture went up in flames. Around me, everyone stood stunned.

[P148]
I watched the livestock flee in every direction and muttered, “…Someone will definitely come out now.”

[P149]
“…That wasn’t supposed to happen.”

[P150]
Wasn’t supposed to happen, my ass. We were fucked.

[P151]
I stared miserably at the burning pasture.

[P152]
*Roooar!*

[P153]
A savage roar rang out, and a figure appeared beyond the hill on the far side of the flames.

[P154]
[^1]: *The Sound of the Bell* is a Korean documentary film about an elderly farmer and his ox.

[P155]
[^2]: Majang-dong is a Seoul district known for its livestock and meat markets.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

A fence around the vast grounds, and a wooden sign someone had scrawled on in a clumsy hand.

[P14]
Not a high, sturdy wall or an iron gate. A fence. Just a fence.

[P15]
*…Wait. This is a sect?*

[P16]
Same thought, different reason.

[P17]
The fence wasn’t even intact.

[P18]

[P19]
“Elder Namho, surely this isn’t really…”

[P20]
“You’re asking if it’s the Nanman Beast Palace?”

[P21]
“Ah, yes.”

[P22]

[P23]
“Can you read?”

[P24]
“Of course.”

[P25]
“Then read that sign. No, perhaps I’d better read it for you.”

[P26]

[P27]
“Nan. Man. Beast. Palace.”

[P28]
“…”

[P29]

[P30]

[P31]

[P32]
“Captain, shouldn’t we call this the Nanman Ranch instead of the Nanman Beast Palace? All I see are fences.”

[P33]

[P34]
“This is my first time here, so I can’t say I know much about the Nanman Beast Palace, but… it does seem a little lacking for a palace.”

[P35]
Song Ilseom and Sama Pyo, who had been watching in silence, each weighed in.

[P36]
“There’s certainly something strange about it.”

[P37]
“As Hyuk Mujin said, the lack of people bothers me. I don’t see any other pavilions or buildings, either. What do you think, Taishan?”

[P38]
“My lord. Taishan is hungry. Can Taishan eat that mushroom?”

[P39]
Sama Pyo shook his head at once.

[P40]
“No.”

[P41]
“Then the cow? That cow walking over there looks tasty.”

[P42]
“You’re the Young Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate, aren’t you? Do me a favor and shut that brute’s mouth. If I hear one more word, I think I’ll burst a blood vessel and die.”

[P43]
“…I understand.”

[P44]
“One more thing. Every blade of grass and every animal you can see belongs to the Nanman Beast Palace. Please remember that. And remember I’m about to burst a blood vessel.”

[P45]
Looking considerably older than he had a moment ago, Namho gave Sama Pyo that stern warning, then pointed across the vast grounds.

[P46]
“I understand why you’re confused, but I never said this place *was* the Nanman Beast Palace.”

[P47]
“What? You said exactly that a moment ago.”

[P48]
“No, I didn’t.”

[P49]
“Ah. Have you gone senile?”

[P50]
“…”

[P51]
His expression darkened so quickly that it seemed certain. I gave him a sympathetic look.

[P52]
“Oh dear. Still, I’m sure you’ll be all right. Someone close to me suffered from the infirmities of old age too, and he’s almost completely recovered.”

[P53]
“Three things. First, I do not suffer from the infirmities of old age. Second—and I ask only because you’ve made me curious—how did this acquaintance of yours recover?”

[P54]
“He Returned to Youth.”

[P55]
“…An excellent method. Apart from the fact that I’m an eighty-year-old man who’s never learned martial arts.”

[P56]
“Isn’t eighty when life begins?”

[P57]
“I’d like to end *your* life here, but I lack the strength.”

[P58]
Namho swallowed his anger and went on.

[P59]
“Third, what I said before still stands. I never said this place *was* the Nanman Beast Palace. I said the Nanman Beast Palace begins *here*.”

[P60]
“Oh.”

[P61]
Similar words, very different meanings. Now that I understood, I asked, “So what is this place?”

[P62]
“One of the lands under the Nanman Beast Palace’s rule. Unlike the rest of Nanman, it’s governed directly by the Palace Lord. Does that make more sense?”

[P63]
“Like the Emperor appointing vassal kings and City Lords throughout the realm. This place is effectively the capital.”

[P64]
“Exactly. Of course, the Palace Lord doesn’t have the authority of the Son of Heaven, and Nanman’s tribal chiefs have more authority than City Lords.”

[P65]
Ju Hwaran, who had been listening, gave a quiet exclamation.

[P66]
“Now that you mention it, I remember reading something like that in my grandfather’s records. He wrote that Nanman was a single kingdom, and the Nanman Beast Palace was like an enormous ranch spanning five counties.”

[P67]
“As expected of the Escort King’s granddaughter. But even Great Hero Ju Gongsan never crossed this fence. People who aren’t of Nanman’s ethnic groups aren’t allowed inside.”

[P68]
“It’s that strict?”

[P69]
“It is.”

[P70]
If Namho was telling the truth, even the Sichuan Tang Clan—a sect as closed to outsiders as any in the world—had to yield to the Nanman Beast Palace.

[P71]
I shook my head and looked past the seemingly endless fence and pasture.

[P72]
“But we need to get in.”

[P73]
“Yes.”

[P74]
“Is there another way? Since you’re Miao, perhaps you can enter…”

[P75]
“I said outsiders aren’t allowed in. I don’t recall saying it was easy for the local peoples, either.”

[P76]
“Oh.”

[P77]
“Here, I’m nothing more than an ordinary, powerless old Miao man. If Dark Heaven hadn’t reached its claws across the world, and you hadn’t come looking for me, I would have quietly lived out my days… You son of a bitch!”

[P78]
I flinched at his sudden shout.

[P79]
“Elder Namho, why are you calling yourself that? What’s wrong with quietly living out your days?”

[P80]
“Not me! That bastard! Catch that fucking son of a bitch!”

[P81]
At Namho’s frantic yell, we turned.

[P82]
A huge backside was crawling over the fence. Beyond it, a yellow calf grazed peacefully.

[P83]
“Oh. Oh, no.”

[P84]
“Surely he isn’t…”

[P85]
“When did that bastard get over there?”

[P86]
“Young Hero Tae!”

[P87]
“Taishan!”

[P88]
Sama Pyo’s cry came last. Taishan flinched.

[P89]
*Moo?*

[P90]
The calf sensed something was wrong and jerked its head up. Taishan was already close. An exclamation mark seemed to appear in its large, clear eyes as its not-yet-fully-grown hooves dug into the grass.

[P91]
*Pat-pat-pat!*

[P92]
A quick decision and an attempt to flee—but Taishan was a step faster.

[P93]
“Beef! Stop right there!”

[P94]
With that determined shout, his enormous body flew through the air.

[P95]
The calf was no tiger or leopard. How was it supposed to evade a Peak master who’d decided to catch it?

[P96]
Taishan landed with a heavy *thud*, and the calf pinned beneath him screamed.

[P97]
*Moooooo!*

[P98]
It was a plaintive cry, enough to bring tears to your eyes just hearing it. But after days of forced marches and meager rations, all it did was make Taishan’s mouth water.

[P99]
“Taishan! Beef!”

[P100]
“Get that bastard off it!”

[P101]
Before Namho finished shouting, I’d vaulted the fence and reached Taishan.

[P102]
I grabbed him.

[P103]
“Let go! Beef tartare!”

[P104]
“Stop it, you heartless lunatic. Haven’t you seen *The Sound of the Bell*?”[^1]

[P105]
“No!”

[P106]
“…Ah.”

[P107]
Well, of course he hadn’t.

[P108]
That made sense, but it changed nothing. I seized him by the back of the neck and hauled him away.

[P109]
His mountain-sized body toppled backward. The beef—no, the calf—scrambled to its feet and ran.

[P110]
*Thud-thud-thud-thud!*

[P111]
Grass flew up beneath its hooves, dust rising in its wake. Taishan watched its rump disappear beyond the pasture and muttered mournfully.

[P112]
“No. Taishan’s rump meat…”

[P113]
*Was this guy born in Majang-dong or something?*[^2]

[P114]
While I questioned his origins, Namho erupted.

[P115]
“You brute!”

[P116]
“Elder Namho, calm down. Please.”

[P117]
“How am I supposed to calm down? I warned you again and again not to touch anything on the Nanman Beast Palace’s land! That great hulking glutton ignored every word I said and went after a calf?”

[P118]
Sama Pyo hurried between Namho and Taishan.

[P119]
“I’m sorry, Elder Namho. I looked away for just a moment, and… Taishan, apologize to him at once.”

[P120]
Taishan looked Namho straight in the eye.

[P121]
“Taishan is hungry.”

[P122]
“That fucking bastard. Let go of my hand. Let go! Are you going to let go or not? Did you think I spent over fifty years getting bitten by mosquitoes in Nanman just to see this?”

[P123]
Life really did begin at eighty. Namho had never learned martial arts, yet the aura he was giving off might have made even Jeok Cheongang back down for once.

[P124]
The old Hidden Shadow Pavilion agent raged like an active volcano for another fifteen minutes before finally calming down.

[P125]
“Whew. I’m fine now. Let go of my hand.”

[P126]
“Are you sure?”

[P127]
“My insides have turned a full circle, but I’m not about to die.”

[P128]
A 180-degree turn would have been a problem. A full 360? That was fine.

[P129]
I nodded to Hyuk Mujin, and he released Namho’s hand. Namho sighed, looking as though he were on his deathbed.

[P130]
“At least nothing happened in the end. If someone from the Nanman Beast Palace had seen that, we’d have been in trouble before we even began.”

[P131]
At another sect in the Central Plains, someone might have thought, *It’s only one cow.* But cultures and people differed. Just as nomads treasured their horses like their own lives, livestock was a valuable asset here, where the boundaries between tribes were sharply drawn and relations between them often strained.

[P132]
*It’s called the Nanman Beast Palace, after all.*

[P133]
Even the name sounded animal-friendly. Namho had warned us from the start not to touch anything for a reason.

[P134]
“So what do we do now?” Hyuk Mujin asked. “We can’t wait here forever for someone to show up.”

[P135]
“Entering the Nanman Beast Palace’s territory without permission would cause trouble. We’ll have to find another way.”

[P136]
Namho reached into his bundle and took something out.

[P137]
“What’s that?”

[P138]
“An emergency signal firework. If it goes off, someone should at least come out to investigate.”

[P139]
He smiled confidently and lit the fuse with his fire striker.

[P140]
*Crackle.*

[P141]
The fuse burned rapidly toward the end. Then, with a tremendous noise, the firework shot upward.

[P142]
*Fwoooosh—boom!*

[P143]
The problem was that its sparks fell onto the pasture instead of scattering harmlessly in the air.

[P144]
“…Huh?”

[P145]
“…Huh?”

[P146]
*Whoooosh—roar!*

[P147]
The pasture went up in flames. Around me, everyone stood stunned.

[P148]
I watched the livestock flee in every direction and muttered, “…Someone will definitely come out now.”

[P149]
“…That wasn’t supposed to happen.”

[P150]
Wasn’t supposed to happen, my ass. We were fucked.

[P151]
I stared miserably at the burning pasture.

[P152]
*Roooar!*

[P153]
A savage roar rang out, and a figure appeared beyond the hill on the far side of the flames.

[P154]
[^1]: *The Sound of the Bell* is a Korean documentary film about an elderly farmer and his ox.

[P155]
[^2]: Majang-dong is a Seoul district known for its livestock and meat markets.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
